purpose: One additive Workbench host-claim capacity question; separate from the unchanged frozen32 evaluation and its metrics.

questions.query: Why can a valid Workbench landscape fail at 6,554 rectangles when source construction allows 32,768, and does omitting geometry from the host claim skip validation?
facts: A rectangle has five integer words, so 6,554 rectangles exceed the unrelated 32,768-values-per-Array host-observation limit while remaining within the 32,768-rectangle Workbench source budget.

The Draft/HOLD candidate validates the complete definition and passes all ordered rectangles unchanged to native preparation; only the unverified observation copy omits an oversized Workbench rectangle Array.

The projection discloses its status, omitted field, encoding, exact word and rectangle counts, and the canonical SHA-256 of the complete validated definition. It is not an installation acknowledgement or complete executed-host proof.
Smaller Workbench claims, strict non-Workbench validation, native limits, failure atomicity and Setup-v2/generated-start-v1 persistence remain unchanged.

Installed bridge capacity is independent: an older 4,096-rectangle binary is not upgraded by the claim repair. Actual platform native/Rapier progression and fresh-process reopening require separately recorded execution.
